  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: `_branch_head_sha` depends on URI-encoded branch names for GitHub ref lookups.
  WHY: Branches containing slashes are only resolved if GitHub/server routing decodes the encoded path segment correctly, making the lookup fragile.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:2670-2688 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_branch_head_sha` does not have robust retry/backoff handling for transient GitHub failures.
  WHY: A transient 429/502/503 or empty SHA can return an empty value, which breaks the revalidate audit path and suppresses memory-event recording.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3670-3862,11794-11826 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Eager draft PR creation and validation-status updates are not serialized, so concurrent poll ticks can race.
  WHY: Separate list/check/create and fetch/patch sequences can overlap, producing duplicate draft PRs or stale validation-status content.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:5680-5690 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: `gh pr ready` can fail when the token lacks push permissions.
  WHY: The promotion path warns and returns 1 on permission errors, so final merge stalls for read-only or fork tokens.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3827-3865 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: PR body PATCH failures are swallowed and retried forever.
  WHY: Callers append `|| true`, so oversized or rejected validation-status updates never converge and keep warning on every poll tick.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3812-3850 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The validation-status updater does unnecessary API and CPU work when the block is unchanged.
  WHY: The function fetches PR JSON and runs the Python rewrite before the equality check short-circuits.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:10898-11185 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The rapid `/revalidate` dedup window relies on a fragile comment-boundary heuristic.
  WHY: Edited or malformed comments can break boundary detection and let repeated `/revalidate` commands bypass the 5-minute guard.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:11095-11105 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: Revalidate audit events can lose source-comment provenance when comment JSON fields are missing.
  WHY: If both `.html_url` and `.id` resolve empty, the memory record writes null source fields and the event is no longer traceable to the triggering comment.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3732-3820 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: `build_eager_pr_validation_status_block` reads `TRACKING_NUM` from ambient shell scope instead of an explicit input.
  WHY: A missing or shadowed variable can render the draft PR body with `#0` or an empty tracking reference.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3729-3850 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The validation-status body rewrite can corrupt the PR description on edge cases.
  WHY: Malformed overlapping blocks and unescaped `next_action_override` text can strip trailing PR-body content during the regex substitution path.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3857-3865 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: A heredoc failure can turn the rewritten PR body into an empty string and still be PATCHed.
  WHY: The later equality check treats the empty rewrite as a change, so the function can overwrite the PR description with an empty body.
- agents.md:197-204 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]

  WHY: `REVALIDATE_DEDUPED` and `REVALIDATE_EVENT_RECORDED` are not listed, so log consumers relying on `agents.md` can miss or misclassify those events.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 5660-5663 (the `pr_draft = "true"` guard in `finalize_integration_merge_if_needed`)
  Problem: A pre-existing final PR created before this change (without `--draft`) will have `pr_draft = "false"`, bypassing the new readiness gate. If the tracking issue does not yet carry `ai:ready-to-merge` or `ai:validated`, and validation is enabled, the PR can fall through to the mergeability check and be squash-merged before the readiness condition is met.
  Why it fails at runtime: A project with a legacy open non-draft final PR that hasn't reached `ai:ready-to-merge` is merged prematurely, violating the "promote draft to ready only when tracking issue reaches ai:ready-to-merge" contract. The backward-compatibility fallbacks (`tracking-validated-legacy`, `validation-disabled-legacy`) only fire when the label already exists — they do not cover the unvalidated-legacy-PR case.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: ~3690-3715 (`ensure_eager_final_pr`)
  Problem: The function first lists existing PRs via `gh pr list`, then creates a new one via `gh pr create --draft` if none found. There is a TOCTOU race: between the list and the create, a concurrent poll tick (cron + revalidate dispatch + stall recovery) can create a PR on the same head/base pair.
  Why it fails at runtime: Two draft PRs can exist with identical head/base/title. The state file records only the one returned by the faster `ensure_eager_final_pr` call. The orphaned duplicate PR persists indefinitely, consuming reviewer attention and creating confusion in the repo's PR list. The `gh pr create` call itself would succeed rather than 422 because GitHub does not enforce uniqueness on head/base PR pairs.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: 5678-5680 (`gh pr ready` call) and 3834-3860 (`update_eager_pr_validation_status_section` PR body PATCH)
  Problem: The draft→ready promotion and the validation-status body update are not guarded by any distributed lock or idempotency key. Concurrent poll ticks on the same tracking issue can both observe `pr_draft = true`, both evaluate the readiness gate, and both attempt `gh pr ready`. The second call would succeed silently (marking an already-ready PR as ready is a no-op), but the body-update race can interleave: one tick writes the pre-promotion status block while another writes the post-promotion block, producing stale display.
  Why it fails at runtime: An observer sees the validation status section flip between "awaiting readiness" and "validation passing — final merge may proceed" across ticks, or briefly showing stale data. The merge gate itself is not affected (the PR is ready), but the operator-facing dashboard is inconsistent. The probability is low (requires two ticks within the same ~30s window) but nonzero because the poller runs every 5 minutes and revalidate/recovery paths can trigger mid-cycle dispatches.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Line or code reference: Callers at lines 5674, 5692, 11824 (all append `|| true` to `update_eager_pr_validation_status_section`); function body at 3856-3862
  Problem: The `update_eager_pr_validation_status_section` function returns 1 on API failure (e.g., 422 oversized body, 403 token scope, transient 502). Every caller appends `|| true`, suppressing the error. Nothing prevents retrying the same failing body update on every poll tick indefinitely.
  Why it fails at runtime: A persistent failure (example: a very large PR description plus validation status block approaching the ~65K character PR body limit) would emit a `::warning::` on every 5-minute poll tick forever, filling logs and never converging. The draft PR body would permanently show stale or absent validation status.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: "Refactor the eager-final-PR path so the poller can ensure a draft integration PR exists as soon as the integration branch is ahead of default, even before validation passes."
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh (the wave-status block at ~11794-11826)
  Evidence of absence: Implemented. The eager-final-PR block at lines 11794-11826 creates/refreshes the draft PR whenever `CWS_AHEAD_BY > 0`. The test `test_integration_ahead_creates_and_reuses_eager_draft_pr_before_validation_complete` confirms this.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: N/A — requirement satisfied.
- Requirement: "Add/update an idempotent validation-status section in that draft PR and only promote the draft to ready when the tracking issue reaches `ai:ready-to-merge`."
  Expected change site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh (`build_eager_pr_validation_status_block`, `update_eager_pr_validation_status_section`, `finalize_integration_merge_if_needed`)
  Evidence of absence: Implemented. The `<!-- VALIDATION_STATUS_V1 -->` block is built and updated. The readiness gate at lines 5660-5698 checks `ai:ready-to-merge`, `ai:validated` (legacy), or `ENABLE_VALIDATION != true` (legacy) before promoting. Test `test_final_merge_promotes_eager_draft_pr_when_tracking_issue_ready_to_merge` confirms. Covered by the CORRECTNESS finding above
